traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.42, 0.36, 0.3], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: a shrub 0.5 m to 2 m tall; FEIS's skunkbush review (as Rhus trilobata, the western variety): 2 to 12 feet (0.6-3.6 m), averaging 4 feet (1.2 m).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: a native woody shrub that achieves a mature height of 5 to 8.2 feet (1.5-2.5 m).

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: a native woody shrub.

traits.woodiness.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: a native woody shrub.

traits.clonal.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: rhizomatous; reproduces clonally by sprouting from the roots and rhizomes, as far as 3.7 m to 4.6 m from the original stem, and by layering where stems touch the ground.

traits.stem_clump.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: typically has a thicket-forming growth habit as a result of prolific layering and sprouting; FEIS's skunkbush review (as Rhus trilobata) gives thickets as large as 9 m across.

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: leaves deciduous and alternate with 3 leaflets.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: leaves deciduous and alternate.

traits.leaf_division.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: leaves with 3 leaflets.

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus trilobata: leaves 3-foliolate, the terminal leaflet larger than the lateral ones (the western variety of R. aromatica).

traits.division_order.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus trilobata: terminal leaflet 3-lobed and coarsely toothed, not divided again.

traits.leaflets.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: leaves with 3 leaflets.

traits.terminal_leaflet.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus trilobata: terminal leaflet 2.5-5 cm. long.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves 5 cm to 10 cm long.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: terminal leaflets are 1.8 to 2.6 inches long (3-6.5 cm); Abrams (1951 p. 51, R. trilobata): terminal leaflet 2.5-5 cm. long, the lateral leaflets smaller.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 4 cm to 9 cm across their lateral leaflets.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: petioles 1 cm to 2.5 cm long, as in the photos.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus trilobata: the lateral leaflets round-ovate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus trilobata: the lateral leaflets scarcely lobed, crenate; the terminal one coarsely toothed.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus trilobata: leaves more or less pubescent on both surfaces.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus trilobata: flowers in short spike-like clusters; FEIS: dense clusters or spikes.

traits.flowering_position.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: flower buds are formed terminally in the summer for flowering the following spring.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: dense clusters or spikes, 0.7 to 2.5 inches (2-6 cm) long.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: 10 to 30 flowers in a spike, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 16537803, 349918686, 71650315, 72173245, 165381048, 42727708, 205904116, 109113316): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: flowers 3 mm to 5 mm across.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus trilobata: flowers yellowish; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: the fruits are hairy drupes.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: FEIS species review, Rhus aromatica: drupes 0.2 to 0.3 inches (5-7 mm) in diameter.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 51, Rhus trilobata: drupe viscid-hirsute, reddish; sRGB by eye.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: flowering March to May, before the leaves (Abrams 1951 p. 51, R. trilobata: flowers appearing before the leaves).

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: drupes ripe June to August.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low, densely and irregularly branched shrub of small three-parted leaves, with short yellowish flower spikes clustered at the bare twig tips in spring.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for fragrant sumac from its sources and the photos the traits cite; the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 1.2 m tall at 12 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the core-species expansion, phase C batch 3 (2026-10-18): sizes and forms from Abrams, FEIS and Dendrology, counts from photos.
